observations: Three photos show a large white plastic tank with a metal cage frame, stacked vertically.
The tank has a blue and black spigot or valve at the bottom front.
The tank appears to be used, with visible dirt, grime, and some scuff marks on the plastic.
The metal cage is gray and shows signs of wear and rust in some areas.
The tank is placed outdoors, likely in a yard or storage area, with other similar tanks visible in the background.
No brand or model markings are visible on the tank in any photo.
The seller claims it is for storing industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals.

claims.claim: To store industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals
claims.evidence: The tank's design and size suggest it can hold liquids, but there is no visible evidence of its intended use or chemical compatibility. The presence of a spigot and cage does not confirm it is for hazardous materials.

risks.risk: The tank may not be suitable for storing hazardous chemicals due to lack of certification or material compatibility.
risks.proof: A close-up of the tank's label or certification mark, or a video showing the tank being filled with a chemical and tested for leaks or degradation.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not suitable for hazardous chemicals

risks.risk: The tank may have internal damage or cracks not visible from the outside.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the interior of the tank, or a pressure test report.

risks.risk: The tank may have been previously used for non-industrial purposes, affecting its suitability.
risks.proof: A photo of the tank's interior showing residue or previous contents.

proof_requests: Close-up of the tank's label or certification mark.
Video or photo of the tank's interior.
Photo of the tank's lid or top, if any.
Proof of the tank's material compatibility with hazardous chemicals.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
